The test image shows a green mango leaf with small, discrete bumps/blister-shaped galls scattered along the leaf surface and margins — the leaf itself remains otherwise healthy green.

**Comparison with references:**
- **Gall_Midge**: Exact match — reference shows same small dark galls protruding from leaf surface and margins on an otherwise green leaf. Same shape, distribution, and size.
- **Bacterial_Canker**: No match — shows angular/jagged necrotic lesions along margins, not raised galls.
- **Sooty_Mould**: No match — black sooty coating across surface.
- **Die_Back**: No match — fully browned/dead curled leaves.
- **Powdery_Mildew**: No match — white powdery patches.
- **Anthracnose**: No match — distorted young leaves with necrotic lesions.
- **Cutting_Weevil**: No match — stripped shoot stubs, no leaf blade present.

The small round blister-shaped galls visible along the leaf margins perfectly match the Gall_Midge symptom description: "round, blister-shaped galls approximately 2–3 mm in diameter on mango leaves, visible on both sides of the leaf."
